references.text: The Lord shows Moses a rock at Horeb where he is to stand, a similar motif with Moses standing on a rock in God's presence.
The continuation of this text where Moses is placed in the cleft of the rock when the glory of the Lord passes by.
Moses is told to speak to the rock, illustrating the rock's significance as a place of God's revelation and presence.
The Lord is referred to as 'the Rock' (הַצּוּר), a metaphor for God's stability and faithfulness.
The Lord is described as 'my Rock' (צוּרִי), a place of refuge and salvation.
Being lifted up on a rock symbolizes God's protection and presence.
The rock that is higher than the psalmist himself represents God as a refuge and safety.
The righteous shall dwell on the heights of the rock, an image of safety in God's presence.
Paul identifies the rock that followed the Israelites with Christ, a typological interpretation of the rock motif.
Both verses emphasize that God's presence makes a physical place holy, requiring reverence and obedience from humanity.
